subject: Fintegral procurement path & champion enablement — next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Caldwell <avery.caldwell@fintegral.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fintegral procurement path & champion enablement — next steps

Hi Avery — thanks again for the demo today, appreciate you walking us through the latency and throughput constraints for the reconciliation use case. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key decision criteria you mentioned:
- Must achieve >30% cost reduction vs current inference spend or show a clear path to it;
- Endpoint latency under 50ms 95th for the nightly batch/interactive mix;
- SOC 2 / security evidence and on-prem or VPC deployment option;
- Pilot needs to be contractually scoped for Q3 start with a commercial pilot PO.

Immediate next steps (proposed mutual action plan — attached):
1) Security questionnaire & evidence: Redwood to deliver SOC 2 artifact matrix + short architecture diagram (we can have the pack to you in 3 business days) — action: Priyom/Rishi;
2) Procurement checklist: Fintegral to share procurement timeline and legal redline owners;
3) ROI one-pager for CFO: Redwood to prepare CFO-facing ROI and topline TCO delta — action: Rishi;
4) Pilot scope draft (success metrics, sample dataset, timeline): Redwood to draft and share for your review by next Wed.

Can you confirm the procurement lead and the ultimate economic buyer so we can tailor the ROI? Also flag any additional security contacts beyond what you mentioned on the call. Attaching a first-pass MAP and an outline for the CFO one-pager so you can share internally.

Attachments: fintegral_mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf (MAP stub)

Thanks — I’ll loop in Rishi and Priyom for the security and ROI items. If it helps, we can do a 30-minute procurement sync next week to walk the checklist with Marcus and legal.

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fintegral procurement path & champion enablement — next steps

Tessa — thanks for the clear recap and the MAP. Quick answers below: 

- Economic buyer: Janelle Park (CFO) — she’ll want an ROI that highlights hard savings to Opex and any headcount deferrals.
- Procurement lead: Marcus Li (procurement) — he manages vendor onboarding and PO timing.
- Security: Samir Desai (Head of InfoSec) — he’ll validate SOC 2 artifacts and ask for additional network diagrams for VPC mode.

Timeline: internal budget approval for pilot expected in ~6 weeks; target pilot start early Q3 (week of Jul 12). If we can provide an ROI and the SOC 2 artifacts within the next 10 business days, that will keep us on track.

Please send the CFO one-pager and ROI template — Janelle prefers a single page with 3 scenarios (conservative/base/upside) and a 12-month NPV. Marcus will schedule a short procurement sync after he reviews your MAP.

Thanks — looping Marcus, Samir and Janelle so they have context.

Best,
Avery Caldwell

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:21:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Fintegral CFO one-pager — draft numbers and talk tracks

Internal note (do not forward to customer yet) — drafting numbers for the CFO one-pager. High-level assumptions below (will turn into scenarios by EOD Monday):

Assumptions:
- Baseline: Fintegral current monthly inference spend = $120k; average latency 85ms (95th).
- Redwood pilot (base case): 40% unit cost reduction, 30ms 95th latency, pilot throughput same as baseline.

Preliminary topline (12-month view):
- Conservative: 20% cost reduction -> annualized savings = $28.8k/mo * 12 = $345.6k; NPV (12m, 8% discount) ~ $336k
- Base: 40% cost reduction -> annualized savings = $48k/mo * 12 = $576k; NPV ~ $560k
- Upside: 55% cost reduction with caching/quantization -> annualized savings = $66k/mo * 12 = $792k; NPV ~ $770k

Talk tracks for CFO (short bullets):
- Direct cost reduction on inference spend (present numbers above) + predictable reserved pricing option for scale.
- Faster time-to-result -> operational benefits (reconciliations completed overnight) that reduce manual review headcount by an estimated 0.5 FTE in base case (quantify if they want).
- Risk mitigation: on-prem/VPC option keeps sensitive data in their control; audit logs and KMS support for compliance.

Next steps: I’ll convert the assumptions into the three scenarios and build a single-slide CFO-ready PDF. Priyom — once you confirm the SOC 2 artifact list I’ll wire up the security callout so the CFO sees compliance is covered. Lauren — can you pull any existing chase metrics from our account playbook that show headcount deferral examples?

I’ll have a polished one-pager morning Monday.

Rishi
Director, GTM Economics, Redwood Inference
